title: Japanese Imperial Era Calendar
intro: Japan's modern imperial era system identifies a date by era name, era year, Gregorian month and day.
structure: The first era year begins on the actual transition date, not necessarily on 1 January, and is called gannen. Subsequent era years increment on the Gregorian New Year.
example: 30 April 2019 was Heisei 31; 1 May 2019 was Reiwa 1. Gregorian 2026 is Reiwa 8.
history: The Gregorian calendar was adopted for Japanese civil use in 1873. The provider covers the modern Meiji, Taisho, Showa, Heisei and Reiwa eras. Era labels remain familiar in official forms and everyday records.
model: The provider uses recorded modern imperial era boundaries and Gregorian month/day arithmetic. Era year equals Gregorian year minus the era's starting year plus one.
limits: Before 1 January 1873 Japanese civil dates were lunisolar. The provider's Gregorian projections for Meiji years 1–5 are not original historical civil notation.
